about: Evidence behind each F1-F6 mark of the paper's table. 'with' runs contain the construct as generated; 'without' runs differ from them by removing it. Each entry is [run in minimal/results.csv, expected status, expected functional_check, substring of error_head or detail]. paper_table.py checks every entry against the records.

marks.claim: Every ap_fixed input stops at parse inside the vendor ap_fixed implementation; the same design with the float option parses.
Every ap_fixed input stops at parse inside the vendor ap_fixed implementation; the same design with the float option parses.
Polygeist asserts while lowering ap_private, and rejects hls::exp on an ap_fixed value; the float designs parse.

AutoSA's Clang front end asserts while reading the headers included through ap_fixed.h, which float designs also include (logs/autosa/gemm/headers-only-run.log keeps only those headers and shows the include chain); with the headers removed it parses and builds kernels.
ScaleHLS turns the written file-scope buffers into constant buffers and crashes; with the declarations moved into top() it compiles the design.
HIDA turns the written file-scope buffers into constant buffers and crashes; with the declarations moved into top() it compiles the design.
StreamHLS asserts in its constant matcher on the file-scope buffers; with them moved into top() the matcher passes and the design reaches loop permutation.
The AutoSA inputs keep the buffers at file scope (the patch only removes headers, adds #pragma scop and rewrites +=); AutoSA builds kernels from them.

HIDA rewrites the top-level interface: it passes the one-element output port by value, drops unit dimensions, and adds ports for buffers it moves off chip, so the emitted top() cannot be called as the original. The code itself synthesizes (minimal/synth_unchecked.csv).
ScaleHLS keeps the interface: its output is checked through the original top() call.
StreamHLS keeps the interface: its output is checked through the original top() call.
AutoSA's host code keeps the original top() signature: it is compiled and run through the original call, and fails on values, not on the interface.
HIDA is correct for all six GEMM loop orders.
ScaleHLS silently miscompiles the four orders in which the reduction loop is not innermost; the two others are correct.
StreamHLS crashes in loop permutation on the four orders in which the reduction loop is not innermost; the two others are correct.
AutoSA produces no correct kernel in either of the two loop orders it was given (ijk, ikj).
marks.not_isolated: The two orders give byte-identical kernels (generated_hls/autosa/gemm_i{jk,kj}__autosa/st*/top_kernel.*), so the failure is not caused by loop order; under the caption's definition this mark would be a tick with the failure explained elsewhere.

marks.claim: ScaleHLS crashes on the padding guard around the convolution body; with the guard moved onto the innermost statement it is correct.
HIDA crashes on the padding guard around the convolution body; with the guard moved onto the innermost statement it is correct.
StreamHLS computes wrong results whenever the guard is present, even on the innermost statement; the same unpadded convolution without the guard is correct.
AutoSA rejects the guarded convolution with a non-uniform dependence; the unpadded convolution without the guard yields kernels.
ScaleHLS is correct on the scalar accumulators of RMSNorm and softmax as generated (buffers moved into top() only).
HIDA's C++ emitter cannot print the loop-carried value of a scalar accumulator, so its output does not compile; with one array slot per row it is correct.
StreamHLS crashes on the row reductions in every form tried.
For the scalar accumulator, AutoSA either declares no FIFO or emits a kernel that hangs.
